# XPad for Mac

> XPad is a free, open-source (MIT) Chrome extension that makes Xbox 360-style USB controllers work as a real analog gamepad in browser games on a Mac. These controllers and their 2.4 GHz USB receivers (for example the 8BitDo Ultimate C 2.4G in X-input mode) use Microsoft's XInput protocol, which macOS has no driver for, so Chrome doesn't see them. XPad reads the controller with Chrome's WebUSB in its own tab and presents it to every tab as a standard Xbox 360 gamepad (Gamepad API, "standard" mapping). No driver, no kernel extension, no SIP changes.

- Download: https://github.com/OGskrrt/XPad-for-Mac/archive/refs/heads/main.zip (load the `extension` folder via chrome://extensions › Developer mode › Load unpacked)
- Source: https://github.com/OGskrrt/XPad-for-Mac
- Turkish page: https://ogskrrt.github.io/XPad-for-Mac/tr/

## Key facts

- Works with: wired Xbox 360 controllers and third-party pads/receivers in XInput mode. Tested with 8BitDo Ultimate C 2.4G, nfsu2.xyz and hardwaretester.com.
- Browsers: Chrome and Chromium browsers (WebUSB). Not Safari or Firefox.
- Not needed for: Xbox One/Series, PlayStation and Switch Pro controllers (supported natively).
- The XPad tab must stay open while playing; only one program can hold the controller at a time.
- Privacy: no network access, no analytics.
